title: Can AI assess adult ADHD as accurately as a clinician? The RAVEN study
official: Diagnostic accuracy of an artificial intelligence voice assessment for adult ADHD: a prospective paired study (RAVEN)
summary:
Background and study aims
Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects around 3-4% of adults, and many people wait a long time for an NHS assessment because there are not enough specialist clinicians. Rainbow Diagnostics has developed a computer program (an AI voice assistant) that asks the same kinds of structured questions a clinician asks during an ADHD assessment. Before such a tool could ever be considered for use in care, it must be tested. This study measures how well the AI's conclusions agree with the judgement of a qualified clinician, and how easy, accessible and comfortable people find being assessed by an AI, including how well it builds rapport and whether people would prefer other language options.

Who can participate?
Adults aged 18 or over who are patients of Rainbow Diagnostics: around 50 people who have recently completed an ADHD assessment with a clinician as part of their care, and around 50 people with no ADHD diagnosis who attended the practice for other reasons.

What does the study involve?
Participants who recently had their ADHD assessment complete one extra research activity: a conversation of about 60 minutes with the AI voice assistant from home, within three weeks, plus a short feedback questionnaire. Participants with no ADHD diagnosis have two appointments: a normal assessment with a clinician (about 60 minutes, by video) and then the AI conversation. The AI's results are used for research only - they are not shown to participants or their clinicians and change nothing about anyone's care. Participants receive a 25 GBP voucher for their time.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
There is no direct clinical benefit. Some questions cover personal topics and could be tiring or upsetting; participants can pause or stop at any time and a clinician is available during every AI session. Results will help determine whether AI tools can safely reduce waiting times for ADHD assessment.

Where is the study run from?
Rainbow Diagnostics Ltd (UK); all appointments are remote.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
January 2027 to April 2027.

Who is funding the study?
Rainbow Diagnostics Ltd.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Raja Mohan, raja@rainbowadhd.com

interventions.name: RAVEN AI voice assessment software (Rainbow Diagnostics Ltd), investigational standalone software, version locked for the study

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Aged 18 years or over
2. Patient of Rainbow Diagnostics Ltd
3. Group A: referred for ADHD assessment, ASRS screen positive, completing the routine clinician diagnostic assessment
4. Group B: no known ADHD diagnosis, attended the practice for other reasons, ASRS-negative at recruitment
5. Sufficient spoken English to complete a voice interview
6. Capacity to give informed consent
7. Access to a phone or computer and a private space
Exclusion criteria:
1. Current acute psychiatric crisis or active suicidality
2. Psychotic disorder or major neurocognitive disorder
3. Open safeguarding concern
4. Participation would delay clinically indicated care
5. Inability to complete a spoken interview in English
6. Concurrent participation in interventional research
